title: Born without sight. Scored over 93% anyway. October 20, 2026.
excerpt: From a 1962 border conflict that reshaped India's defense infrastructure for six decades, to New York City's mayor whose mother was born in Odisha, to a tunnel carved through a mountain that's now the widest on Earth - October 20's five stories are about what gets rebuilt, or built for the first time, after a gap is exposed.
bodyHtml:
Every story today traces back to a gap that got closed - a defense infrastructure gap exposed by war, a traffic bottleneck closed by a record-setting tunnel, a university's resources expanded by its most generous gift ever, political distance crossed by two generations of one family, and a gap in sight that didn't stop a 93.2% score.

October 20, 1962: a border conflict began that would reshape how India builds its defenses for the next six decades

Large-scale fighting broke out along India's northern frontier, exposing gaps in border infrastructure and high-altitude logistics that reshaped Indian defense policy - the Border Roads Organisation's expanded mandate and India's push toward domestic defense manufacturing both trace back to lessons from this conflict.

His mother was born in Odisha and studied at Delhi University before Harvard. In 2026, her son became mayor of America's largest city

Zohran Mamdani was sworn in as the 112th Mayor of New York City on January 1, 2026. His mother, filmmaker Mira Nair, was born in Rourkela, Odisha, in 1957, studied at Delhi University, then earned a scholarship to Harvard before directing films including Salaam Bombay! and Monsoon Wedding.

A metal injection molding entrepreneur just gave his old college its largest-ever single gift

Dr. Krishna Chivukula, a 1970 IIT Madras graduate who founded Indo-MIM, donated Rs 228 crore to his alma mater - the largest single donation in the institute's history, funding fellowships and research grants, with an academic building now named in his honour.

India just built the widest underground road tunnel on Earth

The Mumbai-Pune Expressway's new 13.3 km 'Missing Link' bypass, inaugurated May 1, 2026, includes twin tunnels certified by Guinness World Records as the widest underground road tunnel in the world at 22.33 metres, cutting through the Sahyadri mountains to bypass the Khandala Ghat bottleneck.

Born without sight. Scored 93.2% anyway

Isha Jain, a 15-year-old student at Kalyani School in Pune who was born blind, scored 93.2% in her CBSE Class 10 board exams in 2025, including 95% in English, with support from a writer and a resource teacher.

Five stories, one pattern: a defense gap closed over six decades, a mountain tunneled through to close a traffic gap, a university gift that closed a funding gap at record scale, a family's distance from India closed across two generations and a new mayoralty, and a gap in sight that a 93.2% score made irrelevant.
